dedupe_keys.name: ireland s data centre electricity connection policy cru 2021 direction and 2025 decision

description: This policy case follows how Ireland's energy regulator responded to data centres taking a fast-growing share of national electricity. By 2021 the transmission operator EirGrid warned that data-centre load around Dublin threatened security of supply, and in November 2021 the Commission for Regulation of Utilities directed the system operators (CRU/21/124) to offer connections only where consistent with system needs, judged by whether the site was in a constrained area and whether the data centre brought on-site dispatchable generation or storage matching its demand; in practice this acted as a moratorium on new connections in Dublin. On 12 December 2025 the regulator replaced it with a Large Energy Users connection policy (CRU2025236) requiring new data centres to provide generation or storage, on site or nearby, equal to their maximum import, to take part in the wholesale market, and to source at least 80 per cent of annual demand from additional Irish renewable projects, with location-specific grid assessment. The decision notes that data centres used 5 per cent of Irish electricity in 2015, 22 per cent in 2024 and may use 31 per cent by 2034. Coverage: Ireland, 2021 to 2025 with projections to 2034. Format and access: free decision papers and news on the CRU website, with law-firm summaries. Caveats: the regulator did not publish an evaluation of the 2021 direction's effects. Simulation uses: capacity planning of grids with large data-centre loads, scenarios of flexible or self-supplied data centres, and resilience of supply in constrained regions. Related records: JLARC's Virginia study and the NERC load-loss review show the same pressures in the United States.
